details:
This suggestion asks for the creation of components dedicated to individually packaging and baking components of an avatar to avatar parameters

how this will work is you can package assets like separate material / texture varients, clothing items, etc as different bundles that are all referenced by the same avatar asset. when requesting the un-baked version of the avatar, say when copying it from a pedestal, it should allow the user to customize it completely. from there, the avatar should provide a menu where the user can select what they would like to freeze and what they want to be able change at runtime

this allows avatar creators to allow for more extensive customizations of an avatar, while being able to easily bake in the settings that a user would like to retain while minimizing performance impact during runtime

a good example would be you could choose to only be able to toggle between 3 clothing items, and to only use a certain texture for the base model. you can then bake those details ingame such that only the necessary packages are requested and loaded in memory when the avatar is in operation. this drastically reduces the complexity and performance impact of modern avatars without requiring constant streaming of assets and also inefficient memory/performance usage from invisible or otherwise unused and idle assets

you can revert the baking process in order to fully customize again, but the performance ranking will update to reflect this and users will be highly advised to bake their work avatar if they wish to be seen by all users and not impact their performance negatively

another addition which would be paramount would be to apply the parameters for the avatar in the preview menu as well, so you can see exactly what the avatar will be wearing once you switch to it, as long as showing an icon if the avatar has been baked at all

depending on how creators work with this system, they will be able to set up loading of individual clothing items that will be toggled, or loading of an entire outfit onto the avatar. this ensures that the avatar doesnt spawn in naked or anything of the sort for example, and that all the assets that the user will use will be readily available, and none of the assets which they do not have interest in using

there is also the potential that perhaps this approach is not the best, and instead, avatar options should be manually enabled and disabled entirely. for example, the avatar might come with one set of clothes by default, and you can instead swap to another set of clothes by swapping one bundle for another. this will incur an extra cost at runtime if the user chooses to swap items live, but it will greatly reduce the initial download cost of a full, un baked avatar bundle when first customizing the avatar

this overall would greatly increase the performance of customizable public avatars on vrchat, and require less effort from creators to optimize and create several variations of their avatars. it will also allow users a greater understanding of how their complexity relates to the flexibility of their avatars features, and for most casual users, it will make their experience smoother for very little cost on their end
title: Baking Avatar Bundles
